kept.heading: CONSUMERS RETHINK VALUE AS UNCERTAINTY AND INFLATION PERSIST (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Consumers are adopting 3 distinct spending behaviors depending on the purchase. Some pay more for premium experiences and better performance. Others balance quality and convenience against price to get the most from every dollar. Those seeking to limit spending choose cheaper alternatives and promotions while protecting budgets for priorities. These behaviors aren't fixed consumer segments. The same person may splurge in one category while trading down in another depending on the occasion and perceived value.

kept.heading: GOOGLE IS FEEDING RANK TRACKERS POISONED SERPS WITH SWAPPED RESULTS, NOZZLE FINDS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google has been feeding rank trackers fake search results since September 13. Nozzle found that 8.4% of SERPs were affected across 27M results analyzed. The poisoned pages look normal but retain just 22% of their usual sites. This causes tracked top-10 rankings to disappear 60.2% of the time. Social platforms and forums appear more often in these results. SEO teams should cross-check ranking drops against Google Search Console before assuming their rankings have changed.

kept.heading: PR FOR GEO: 4 WAYS IT CAN INFLUENCE AI VISIBILITY (11 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: PR can improve AI visibility by earning citations for original research, reinforcing how third-party publications describe a brand, building backlinks, and increasing brand awareness. Research tied to customer pain points is more likely to earn useful AI citations than data that is merely related to the business. Consistently using the same brand descriptor in pitches and press releases can also help AI associate a company with its intended category. Measure one specific goal by establishing a baseline and tracking the same prompts across AI platforms over time. Media placements alone do not prove an impact on AI visibility, so report coverage separately from changes in citations, mentions, and recommendations.

kept.heading: THE DISABILITY INCLUSION EFFECT (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: In tests with more than 4,500 participants, Ads featuring a model with a disability made people 33% more likely to choose the product. The lift holds even when people are told the brand cast a wheelchair user only to meet regulations. However, it disappears when the ad calls attention to the disability or portrays the person as vulnerable, since the benefit comes from treating a stigmatized group as ordinary customers.

kept.heading: I ANALYZED 1,100+ MARKETING JOB POSTS. THEY'RE STUCK IN 2023 (26 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Companies are treating AI system-building as one specialist's job rather than a baseline requirement for every marketing hire. Every GTM engineer post asks for AI skills, compared with 47% of marketing posts overall and just 25% of entry-level ones. Only 6% ask candidates to contribute to the shared skills, context, and agents a team runs on, and only 8% ask for proof of AI use.

For example, “site:jobs.ashbyhq.com (business development OR institutional sales) (crypto OR fintech) (remote OR EMEA OR Europe)” finds relevant roles by title, industry, and location. Swap in different keywords or job boards to fit your search. Verify listings are current and remote roles accept applicants in your country.

dropped.heading: CHECK IF GOOGLE CAN INDEX YOUR CONTENT WITH A SITE: SEARCH (1 MINUTE READ)
dropped.blurb: To check whether Google can index specific content on a page, copy a snippet of text and search site:[URL] [snippet of text] in Google. Check whether the text appears in the result's meta description. If it does, Google can access that content. If no results appear, test a few other snippets to confirm there may be an indexing issue.
